perField.chanceTrust: If data collection doesn't use CHANCE (randomness), we can't trust the conclusions. Look for random selection or random assignment.
perField.popOrSample: POPULATION = ALL items/subjects of interest. SAMPLE = a subset selected from the population.
perField.studyType: EXPERIMENT = treatments are assigned/imposed. OBSERVATIONAL = no treatments imposed, just observe what exists.
perField.canGeneralize: Can we say results apply to the whole population? Only if the sample was RANDOMLY SELECTED from that population.
perField.whyGeneralize: Random selection gives every member of the population a chance to be in the sample, making the sample representative.
perField.canCause: Can we say X CAUSED Y? Only if treatments were RANDOMLY ASSIGNED (which is only possible in experiments).
perField.whyCause: Random assignment balances confounding variables across groups, so differences can be attributed to the treatment.
perField.generalize: RANDOM SELECTION from population → can generalize. No random selection → can only describe those in the study.
perField.causation: RANDOM ASSIGNMENT of treatments → can establish causation. No random assignment (observational) → only association.
perField.srsKey: SRS: every GROUP of n individuals has equal chance. Not just every individual—every possible combination!
perField.stratKey: Stratified: divide into homogeneous groups (strata), then take an SRS FROM EACH stratum.
perField.clusterKey: Cluster: divide into groups (clusters), randomly select SOME clusters, then sample ALL individuals in selected clusters.
perField.stratIdeal: Stratified works when groups are HOMOGENEOUS within (similar inside each group, different between groups).
perField.clusterIdeal: Cluster works when groups are HETEROGENEOUS within (each cluster is like a mini-population).
perField.methodType: Systematic = random start, then every kth individual. Census = everyone in the population (no sampling).
perField.methodId: SRS = random from whole list. Stratified = sample from each group. Cluster = select entire groups. Systematic = every kth.
perField.methodId2: Look for key phrases: 'from each' often means stratified. 'All in selected' often means cluster.
perField.advantage: SRS: simple, unbiased. Stratified: ensures representation, reduces variability. Cluster: practical, cheaper. Systematic: easy to implement.
perField.capMethod: First identify: Was it random? If so, how were individuals or groups selected?
perField.capGeneralize: Was the sample randomly selected from the population? If yes → can generalize. If no → cannot generalize.
perField.capWhy: Random selection allows generalization because every member had a chance to be selected.
perField.studyType2: Were treatments assigned by the researcher (experiment) or did they just observe existing conditions (observational)?
perField.capMethod2: Identify the method of selection (for samples) or assignment (for experiments).
perField.capGen2: Random selection from population → generalizable. Convenience/volunteer → not generalizable.
perField.capCause2: Random assignment → causation possible. No random assignment → only association (even in experiments!).
